about: The phones' sound set (docs/ui.md, "Sound and haptics"): one entry per sound the feedback table in contract/design/tokens.json names, each one file of a CC0 pack kept under src/<pack>/ beside the pack's License.txt, or of Pluxia's own synthesised pack (its `synth`, MIT, slice 65), whose sources tools/sound.py makes itself (never Sonniss, whose licence bars supplying its sounds as sound effects in a public tree, and never CC BY). tools/sound.py trims each source's silent ends, brings its true peak to processing.truePeakDb, adds its gainDb (0 or less) and writes apple/iOS/Sounds/<id>.caf and android/phone/src/main/res/raw/<id>.ogg; receipts.json records what it built. A short sound lasts maxMs.short or less, a jingle maxMs.jingle. The watches play no sound. Picked 2026-10-03 from durations and spectra (nobody listened yet; slice 19 tunes them on the phones): a phone speaker gives little below about 400 Hz, so each pick keeps its body above it, close aside (see its why). Each pack's credit is the line the Acknowledgements page shows; creditRequired says whether its licence asks for one.

voices.about: The voice's takes on the phones (docs/plan.md slice 1, "The voice"; David, 2026-10-12: the phones play the addon's audio): every take tools/voice/clips.json names in one of families, its id's part before the first dot: the callouts (2026-10-09), the cadence lines, the legends' lines, the counts (the rep count's numbers and the holds' and timers' marks, every count.<n> the game says; 2026-10-09), "Switch sides." (side.switch, said as a side move's other side's countdown starts), the pace ask's question (ask.pace, said as the ask opens; slice 42) and the move lines (a move's name and cue as the game says them at its Ready); the guides stay the game's alone (the week's omen's cues, omen.<key>, went on 2026-11-03). Each is the addon's own recording in the game's voice (Media/Voice/<id>.ogg; its licence the ledger's voice row), written as apple/iOS/Sounds/<name>.<iphone> (caf: IMA4 at the takes' rate; m4a: AAC-LC at about aacKbps kbit/s from macOS's own encoder, for the move lines, which as IMA4 would add about 32 MB to the iPhone app) and, byte for byte, android/phone/src/main/res/raw/<name>.ogg, the name the id with underscores for its dots (move_inverted_row, count_150); each lasts its family's maxMs or less (the longest move line 12.2 s, 2026-10-12). None is a feedback sound: in their own pumps the phones say them where the game does.

pluxia-ticks.title: QuestPump's ticks
pluxia-ticks.author: Pluxia GmbH
pluxia-ticks.synth: tools/sound.py synthesises each source itself from its entry's `synth` (seeded white noise through a band-pass biquad under two exponential ramps, the mockup's Web Audio voice Ticks of 2026-11-03), the same bytes on every run; License.txt is the repository's LICENSE
pluxia-ticks.credit: Ticks synthesised by Pluxia GmbH for QuestPump, MIT

sounds.role: a soft stone click: PrimaryButton, SecondaryButton, FramedIconButton
sounds.why: a dry click that falls 20 dB within 10 ms, its body at 0.4-1 kHz rather than in the treble

sounds.role: an action-bar button change, softer than tap
sounds.why: a 40-ms blip at about 0.6 kHz, three-quarters of it at 0.4-1 kHz, 3 dB under tap

sounds.role: a switch flips or a side tab changes: a two-state click, softer than tap
sounds.why: a switch's press and release: two clicks 108 ms apart at 1.0 and 0.9 kHz, each 2-5 dB under tap's energy at -15 dB

sounds.role: a window or page opens: one page turn for every window until slice 19 tunes the set
sounds.why: the shortest page turn (230 ms), paper noise at 2.5-6 kHz; bookOpen's thud sits below 400 Hz

the same book closing (230 ms), a low thump that pairs with open; it breaks the 400-Hz rule above: 78 % of its energy lies below 400 Hz (70 % at 200-400 Hz), more than bookOpen's 74 %, so slice 19 decides it by ear

sounds.role: a countdown digit, each of a timed move's last five seconds and a timer's mark the voice does not say
sounds.why: a 20-ms tick, less shrill than tick_001 (half its energy above 6 kHz against two-thirds)
a struck ding at 1.9 kHz ringing 280 ms, the brightest steady tone; bong_001 lies wholly below 400 Hz

sounds.role: a move done: a short low chime
sounds.why: the lowest confirmation chime (two notes, about 0.4 then 1.2 kHz, 290 ms), under go's ding

sounds.role: one second of a hold landing in its bar during the seconds pour (slice 65): a soft dry tick, fixed in pitch, many in a row
sounds.why: Rapha's pick of 2026-11-03 among four voices (Ticks over Tick and chime, Gold chink and Abacus): an 18-ms noise burst at 3.8 kHz, Q 2.5, above a phone speaker's floor and soft enough to repeat up to 35 times a second; 4.5 dB under pour_post, as its peak of 0.12 sat under the post's 0.2

sounds.role: the pour passing the hold bar's goal or best post (slice 65): a double tick
sounds.why: two 26-ms bursts 70 ms apart at 3.4 kHz, a little lower and fuller than the tick, so a post reads as a step in the run

sounds.role: the pour reaching the top of the step's range (slice 65): a triple tick under the full bar's flash
sounds.why: the post's double tick with a third burst 70 ms on, for the bar's last post

sounds.role: a record: a short rising jingle; the day reel's end on a day with a record or an unlock (slice 45, at the reel's gainDb)
sounds.why: pizzicato strings rising D-E-F#-G in 0.8 s

sounds.role: a level-up: the fanfare jingle; the day reel's end on a best day (slice 45, at the reel's gainDb)
sounds.why: the same strings in a six-note run up from C4 to A#4 in 0.95 s, longer and higher than record

sounds.role: a new title's toast: a short bright flourish
sounds.why: a steel pan rising a fifth (D#4, A#4) and ringing 0.91 s; a 400-Hz high-pass takes 1.6 dB off it, 4.1 off the pizzicato

sounds.role: a reward chip's reveal: a soft shine rising in pitch; the day reel's number popping at its total (slice 45, at the reel's gainDb)
sounds.why: a soft tone gliding up from 1.1 to 1.5 kHz in 210 ms, the lowest maximize rise, short enough for four

sounds.role: a Starter or Common step unlocked, or a step Rekindled, a hold passing its goal and a catch-up's count past last time's: the game's small chime (win)
sounds.why: a small struck bell with two partials, 97 ms trimmed, its centroid at 2.2 kHz and its body 39 dB above what lies under 400 Hz; shorter and plainer than go's 280-ms ding, apart from reveal's glide and done's two notes (picked 2026-10-06 from the spectra, slice 29)

sounds.role: an Uncommon step unlocked: a brighter chime
sounds.why: the same bell's higher strike, 92 ms trimmed, its centroid at 2.8 kHz, so Uncommon sounds a step brighter than unlock and stays under the jingles Rare and above play (picked 2026-10-06 from the spectra, slice 29)

sounds.role: an error (pairing, purchase, a refused backup file): a dull low knock
sounds.why: a 105-ms knock falling from about 375 to 190 Hz, its body at 0.4-1 kHz so a phone speaker plays it
